newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Meralco H1 net called disappointing.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Meralco H1 net called disappointing.

text.p: The Manila Electric Co (Meralco) on Friday posted 6.6 percent growth in net profits for the first half at 2.53 billion pesos, but analysts said that figure fell below expectations.
Several analysts said they would lower profit forecasts for the utility for the year.

"It's quite disheartening. The second quarter is usually a strong one because of the summer season. It will surely weigh down sentiments on Meralco," said Gene Gabriel, analyst at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Meralco reported a 6.4 percent rise in kilowatt-hour (kw/h) sales for the first half to 9.04 billion kwhs from 8.5 billion kwhs.

"Sales were dismal considering that the second quarter is a saving grace as people use more electricity during the summer months. I will have to lower my earnings forecast for the year," Guoco Securities research head Saturnino Mejia said.

Anscor-Hagedorn Securities vice-president for research Noel Reyes said he was expecting a much higher rise in net income for the first half and attributed the lower profits growth to an unexpected booking of labour expenses.
Meralco said second-quarter net income was affected by the labor expense adjustment, which resulted from a Department of Labour wage award in December last year. It did not elaborate.
For the second quarter, Meralco said its net income rose 5.3 percent to 1.43 billion pesos (US$50.23 million) from 1.36 billion a year ago.

Meralco earlier said the labour department approved a collective bargaining agreement with the 4,400-member employees union that will cost the company two billion pesos over two years. Meralco has sought a review of the agreement.
Brokerages Sun Hung Kai Securities and Anscor-Hagedorn Securities also said they would downgrade their full-year earnings forecast for Meralco.

An earlier Reuters poll of seven brokerages showed that for the first six months of the year, Meralco was expected to earn 2.84 billion pesos. For the full year, the utility was seen making 6.61 billion in profits.
Guoco's Mejia said the peso depreciation could affect Meralco.
"Although Meralco has a low foreign loan exposure and they can pass on the cost of a weakened peso, a higher rate would mean that people may conserve more," said Mejia.
Angping & Associates Securities analyst Alexis Cabel said the power firm's sales volume growth for the second half must exceed the first six months' figure for Meralco to meet full year targets.

Meralco president Manuel Lopez earlier said he expected electricity sales to grow by at least 9.5 percent this year on prospects the country would sustain its solid economic growth of 6.94 percent in 1996.
Meralco A shares on Friday settled 50 centavos lower at 82.50 pesos while its B shares fell two pesos to 127 pesos. Conversion $1 =28.47 pesos
